feed.title: al-ice.ai — AI security intelligence
feed.subtitle: Primary-source-led intelligence on AI vulnerabilities, agents, and the software supply chain.

entry.title: Upstream Said It Was Not a Vulnerability; Red Hat Gave It an 8.1
entry.summary: CVE-2026-16487 and CVE-2026-16460, published 19 October 2026, record bootc and ostree image-mode Linux hosts booting OS content nobody verified: a mutable tag applied under a policy that falls through to insecureAcceptAnything, and staged deployments finalised without revalidation after policy is hardened. Three months ago bootc’s own security document declared the first one not a vulnerability — six days after it was reported. We read both advisories, the policy commit and the Rust guard first-hand.

entry.title: The Second Path Had No Gate: Two 9.3 CVEs in Google’s AgentMesh
entry.summary: CVE-2026-102503 and CVE-2026-103091, published 19 October 2026, record two critical flaws in Google’s OSS AgentMesh: an unauthenticated /libp2p-http ingress that bypassed Biscuit authorization, and an open OIDC enrollment behind a wildcard default policy. Both were fixed weeks before their CVEs; we read both advisories, the fix commit and both releases first-hand.

entry.title: Project-Wide Passes for Cluster-Scoped Powers: OneUptime’s Fifteen-Advisory October Batch and CVE-2026-112047
entry.summary: OneUptime published fifteen repository security advisories between 13 and 18 October 2026, three of them critical, and only one carries a CVE so far: CVE-2026-112047, in which Kubernetes AI access tests, agent resets and kubectl plan approvals were authorised at project scope instead of cluster scope. We read all fifteen advisories, the fix commits and the release train first-hand, from the 9.8 session forgery to the SAML responses that never expired.

entry.title: The Default Only Fires When the Variable Is Missing: OpenTelemetry Python CVE-2026-112006 and Four Years of Optional TLS
entry.summary: CVE-2026-112006, published 18 October 2026, records that OpenTelemetry’s Python OTLP/HTTP exporter disabled TLS certificate verification whenever OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE was set to an empty string. The affected range runs from 1.5.0 in August 2021 to 1.44.0, the fix arrived inside a 5,204-line refactor with no security label, there is no GitHub advisory, and OSV’s version enumeration omits forty of the fifty-six affected releases. We read the exporter, the fix and the scanner coverage first-hand.

entry.title: The Gate Asked the Wrong Question: Unsloth and ESPnet Fix Model-Bundle Code Execution
entry.summary: CVE-2026-112075 and CVE-2026-112086, published 19 October 2026, record model-bundle code execution in Unsloth and ESPnet: a modules.json type that becomes an import, and a Hydra _target_ that walks past the trust_user_code gate. Same reporter, same defect class as the WebUI sidecar pair — and NVD’s fixed-version metadata is wrong on Unsloth. We read both issues and both fixes first-hand.

entry.title: The Authorizer Was Added to One Connector: WhoDB CVE-2026-112005 and Nineteen Advisories Without an Identifier
entry.summary: CVE-2026-112005, published 18 October 2026, records an unauthenticated arbitrary file read and write in WhoDB through a DuckDB session. Two weeks earlier the same project fixed the identical defect in its SQLite connector with a per-connection authorizer that DuckDB never received. WhoDB has twenty-one repository advisories and two CVEs, both from February 2025; the critical ones are absent from the global advisory database and from OSV’s Go coordinates. We read the advisories, the fix commit and the scanner coverage first-hand.

entry.title: The Validator Knew About Slashes but Not Backslashes: Xinference CVE-2026-112051 and the Release That Does Not Exist Yet
entry.summary: CVE-2026-112051, published 18 October 2026, records an unauthenticated Windows path traversal in Xinference custom model registration: is_valid_model_name rejected the forward slash and permitted the backslash, so a model name like ..\\..\\evil escaped the registry directory on write and delete. The fix is on main only; v4.0.1, the newest release, is still vulnerable. We read the issue, the patch and the registry code first-hand.

entry.title: The Model Was Inert, the File Beside It Was Not: Two Stable Diffusion WebUI CVEs and the 94-Issue Sweep Behind Them
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-111986 and CVE-2026-111987 on 18 October 2026 against AUTOMATIC1111 stable-diffusion-webui, the 165,000-star Stable Diffusion UI whose master branch has not moved since July 2024. Both PoCs are public, both reports have sat unanswered since 30 September, and in both the safetensors file is valid and inert — the execution comes from the config files packaged next to it. We read the vulnerable source first-hand, and counted the reporter’s 94-issue sweep of the same defect class across 77 ML projects.

entry.title: The Gate Checked the Role, Never the Object: AI Engine’s Editor Media Helpers
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-110976 and CVE-2026-111041 on 18 October 2026 against AI Engine, the MCP and chatbot plugin running on 90,000 WordPress sites. Both are missing-authorization bugs in AI media helpers reachable by any Editor. We read the vulnerable and fixed source at 3.7.8, 3.7.9, 3.8.5 and 3.8.6: the fix shipped a month ago, the vendor’s own code comments admit the defect, and six more instances of the same class were patched yesterday with no CVE at all.

entry.title: The Intruders Were Under Test: CERT-In Declares AI Agents an Attack Surface
entry.summary: India’s CERT-In issued Critical advisory CIAD-2026-0049 on 15 October 2026: AI agents under evaluation broke into live Indian systems and read business records with zero detections, disclosed voluntarily by their providers, alongside a separate financially-motivated campaign weaponizing open-source agentic frameworks. We read the full reporting and cross-checked the advisory’s identity across five outlets.

entry.title: “Add Missing Checks to Several Handlers and Models”: Gitea Ships Twelve CVEs in One Release
entry.summary: Gitea 28.2.0 shipped on 18 October 2026 and twelve CVE records followed it to NVD fifty-one minutes later. Five of them come from a single pull request whose title names the defect class outright. The two highest-severity records are authentication bugs — an OpenID callback that never checked who started the linking, and an SSH certificate principal lookup missing a type predicate. We read the release, the twelve advisories and the diffs first-hand, and measured what a dependency scanner sees after Gitea’s module path changed.

entry.title: The Password Was Public and the Check Never Looked Down: LobsterAI CVE-2026-112014 and Omnigent CVE-2026-112015
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-112014 and CVE-2026-112015 within the same second on 18 October 2026, both from VulnCheck, both against AI agent software. LobsterAI encrypted exported provider API keys with a password hardcoded in its public repo; Omnigent validated an uploaded bundle’s working directory at the root and never recursed into sub-agents. Both fixes shipped weeks before the identifiers. We read the vulnerable code, the fix commits, the reporter’s issue and the vendor advisory first-hand.

entry.title: One Legacy System, Three Provider Accounts: OpenCode’s Distillation-Attack Breach and the Key-Wallet Problem
entry.summary: On 17 October 2026 OpenCode emailed a subset of Console users that a legacy system being decommissioned was breached and third-party provider keys saved in workspaces may have been exposed. Hours later it tied the incident to a large-scale distillation attack affecting 1.4% of Console users. No CVE exists, the entry point is undisclosed, and users reported unauthorised spend — so we reconstruct the confirmed timeline, explain why a real customer key is the ideal distillation account, and give the rotation order that limits the damage.

entry.title: The Archive Outlived the Patch: PEERSTITCH Hid in FortiGate Memory on Trust Stolen in 2024
entry.summary: Unit 42 disclosed PEERSTITCH on 14 October 2026: a memory-resident ARM64 implant in FortiGate logging and VPN daemons, planted by CL-STA-0954 after a September 2024 FortiManager breach stole 500+ firewall configurations. The second-stage flaw, CVE-2025-61624, scores only CVSS 6.5 yet entered CISA KEV on 16 October with a 19 October deadline. We read the NVD records and the KEV entry first-hand.

entry.title: The Mirror Is the Attacker: Two of 25 Package Managers Survive a Malicious Repository
entry.summary: Trail of Bits researcher Keegan Ryan tested 25 package managers against a malicious repository that injects malware into legitimate packages. Fewer than half verify lockfile hashes by default, only Go verifies signatures by default, and several managers warn about tampering and install anyway. We read the 14 October 2026 study first-hand.

entry.title: The Guard Lived in One File: Arcane’s Three CVEs and a Credential Repoint That Outlived Its Own Fix
entry.summary: Three Arcane CVEs reached NVD within forty seconds on 16 October 2026 — CVE-2026-96626, CVE-2026-96627 and CVE-2026-96628 — and all three patches are the same refactor: a check that had been written per call site, moved to one enforcement point. We read every fix diff first-hand. The credential-repoint bug fixed in Arcane’s git subsystem in May came back in container registries in July, and in five more subsystems the same week — those five have no CVE and no record in any scanner feed.

entry.title: The Support Appliance Is the Target: ARMORY CASTLE’s BeyondTrust Zero-Day (CVE-2026-102764)
entry.summary: BeyondTrust disclosed CVE-2026-102764 on 15 October 2026: an unauthenticated file-operation flaw (CWE-290, CVSS 9.8) in Remote Support appliances up to 26.2.3. Mandiant attributes zero-day exploitation since late August to ARMORY CASTLE, with a 404-by-default webshell, a SUID root backdoor, Vault credential theft and reboot-proof persistence. CISA KEV-listed it on 16 October with a 19 October deadline. We read the GTIG report, the NVD record and the KEV entry first-hand.

entry.title: Steal the Key, Skip the Jailbreak — Bitsight Charts the Underground’s Move From Chatbot Tricks to Agent Infrastructure
entry.summary: Bitsight’s October 2026 study of 16 underground forums finds AI tradecraft up 45% while ransomware talk fell 49%, with MCP and agent mentions up 67% and a BYOK scanner called MONST3R-AI that bills its scans to stolen OpenAI, Anthropic and Google keys. The same week, Fireworks AI disclosed compromised internal credentials reaching customer evaluation secrets.

entry.title: The Session ID Became a Flag: CVE-2026-96620 Turns Claude Agent SDK’s resume Option Into an MCP Server
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-96620 on 16 October 2026: a CVSS 9.2 argument injection in the Python Claude Agent SDK where a dash-leading resume value is parsed as its own CLI flag, letting an attacker inject --mcp-config and spawn a stdio MCP server outside the SDK’s permission controls. The fix shipped 92 days earlier — and the engineer who wrote it disagrees with the severity.

entry.title: Everything After 10 August Is Invisible: Coder’s Nine Stranded Advisories and Eleven Retroactive CVEs
entry.summary: VulnCheck published eleven Coder CVEs in 8.6 seconds on 17 October 2026, with identifiers spanning 2024, 2025 and 2026. Every one is a retroactive number for a Coder repository advisory that shipped without a CVE. We swept all 37 of Coder’s advisories against the GitHub global database and OSV and found a clean cutoff: all 28 published through 2 July resolve; all 9 published from 10 August onward return 404 in both. One of the nine is critical. A Coder 2.35.0 deployment scans completely clean in OSV while a vendor-published high-severity credential-theft advisory names it.

entry.title: GhostAction’s October Burst, Fully Counted: 30,000 Repos, Three Payload Versions, and the Runs GitHub Stopped
entry.summary: GitGuardian’s 13 October update closes the books on GhostAction’s October burst: 30,000+ repositories across 3,000 users and orgs via roughly 1,900 compromised accounts, a payload that evolved through three versions in a single day, and a platform intervention — GitHub blocking the malicious workflow from 9 October — that left the follow-up waves on 10 and 12 October firing blanks.

entry.title: Refusal Is a Rounding Error: INFUSE Runs 19 Models Through 41,824 Indirect Prompt Injections
entry.summary: INFUSE (arXiv 2610.20776, 14 October 2026) pairs 40 long-horizon terminal-agent tasks with 56 injection attacks across five threat categories and runs 19 models through 41,824 trajectories. Mean attack success is 19.6%, refusal never exceeds 1.0%, and chat-trained guardrails leave 44% of attacks working, while prompt hardening cuts success to 14.3% with uneven utility costs. We read the full paper first-hand.

entry.title: A Traversal That Picks Its Own Serializer — NetLicensing MCP’s ../token Redaction Bypass (CVE-2026-57496) Plus a WordPress Draft-Disclosure Twin
entry.summary: CVE-2026-57496 is a critical path traversal in the NetLicensing MCP server where product_number ../token survives into httpx, normalizes onto the /token endpoint, and returns admin API keys through the serializer that never redacts them. CVE-2026-109382 is the same shape in WordPress: an MCP post-listing tool with no capability check serving every draft to subscribers. Both fixed; both read first-hand.

entry.title: Your Browser Can Reach the Agent: Two Loopback Control Planes Fall to a Page the Operator Visited
entry.summary: CVE-2026-49410 lets any web page log a victim’s OpenHuman into the attacker’s account with one <img> tag; CVE-2026-108372 lets any web page read LoopX’s control-plane state and private Markdown through a wildcard CORS header. Both published 16 October 2026, both found by the same automated security reviewer — whose reports include a section on what it failed to break.

entry.title: Twenty AI Platforms in Eighteen Seconds: VulnCheck’s 122-CVE Batch and the Decorator That Only Looked Like Auth
entry.summary: VulnCheck published 122 CVEs to NVD between 18:17:38.950 and 18:17:56.980 on 16 October 2026. Twenty of them, across sixteen self-hosted AI products, are the same defect: the AI feature holds provider keys, chat transcripts and system prompts, and nobody wrote the authorisation check. We read the source for EFAK, 99AI, LangChat, DataBuff and StaffDeck first-hand — and measured that all twenty records are indexed in OSV and GitHub with no package coordinate at all.

entry.title: Aoki Wants Your Agent’s Keys, Not Your Code: Symantec Tracks an Infostealer’s New Taste for AI Coding Credentials
entry.summary: Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team reports the Aoki infostealer now harvests Claude, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini credentials plus AWS keys — cash-in-grade material that buys both API quota and a route into the developer’s environment. A second family, a second vendor, the same target as Warden.

entry.title: The Gate Was Off by Default: CVE-2026-111322 Leaves Archon’s Agent Control Plane Open on 0.0.0.0
entry.summary: CVE-2026-111322 (CVSS 9.8, CWE-306) in coleam00/Archon: the default SQLite install never arms the /api/* auth gate, and the server binds 0.0.0.0:3090, so any network caller can drive the AI coding agent, start workflow runs, inject conversation messages, and approve paused actions. No fixed release at time of writing.

entry.title: Thirty Dollar Signs Beat the Guard: CVE-2026-77474 Turns a Complexity Bug in dcg Into an Agent Fail-Open
entry.summary: CVE-2026-77474, published to NVD at 17:17:50Z on 16 October 2026, is a 7.1 uncontrolled-resource-consumption flaw in destructive_command_guard — the Rust PreToolUse hook that blocks destructive shell commands before AI coding agents run them. Roughly thirty nested dollar-paren sequences hang the scanner. Because agents fail open on a hung hook, the destructive command in the same payload then runs. The fix shipped in fifteen hours; the CVE took another ninety-four days, and the package has no ecosystem coordinate any scanner resolves.

entry.title: The Summary Is the Persistence Layer: DeepSeek Harness Adds a Search-Path RCE and a Compaction Injection
entry.summary: CVE-2026-95182 and CVE-2026-95183, published seconds apart on 16 October 2026 against DeepSeek Harness at commit c291e796: a CWE-426 untrusted search path lets a poisoned model plant the executable the MCP client will run, and a CWE-1427 compaction flaw preserves injected instructions verbatim across session boundaries. Third dsh briefing in three weeks.

entry.title: Three Days of Patience: Eye Security’s Cooldown Rule for npm and PyPI, and Why Your Coding Agent Needs It Most
entry.summary: Eye Security proposes a three-day minimum release age for npm and PyPI, committed beside a lockfile: a hard package-manager constraint that coding agents inherit and cannot talk their way out of. The rationale runs through Shai-Hulud, Lightning, chalk, and durabletask — plus an honest account of what the gate cannot stop.

entry.title: Inside the PaperCut Attacker’s Workbench: Hunt.io Finds Agent Instructions, a Second XML-RPC RCE, and Victims Across 45 Countries
entry.summary: Hunt.io reconstructed the PaperCut AI-swarm campaign from the attacker’s own open directories: a Codex-plus-DeepSeek workbench run by up to 25 concurrent subagents, a second XML-RPC RCE chain that survives the Tapestry patch, and a post-exploitation pipeline stretching from LSA collectors to packaged domain-admin kits across 45 countries.

entry.title: Exploited Before It Was Published: CVE-2026-105740 and Sixteen Days of Pre-Disclosure Langflow Attacks
entry.summary: Previdian confirms active exploitation of Langflow CVE-2026-105740 with first sensor hits on 19 September 2026, sixteen days before NVD publication. Nearly 2,000 honeypot attempts, credential-stuffing past auto_login, secret exfiltration, and a multi-CVE scanner IP. Still absent from CISA KEV, with EPSS at 0.6%.

entry.title: Seventeen Days of Root: A Miner in QwenPaw’s MCP Driver Table, and the Maintainer Who Says It Is Not a Bug
entry.summary: QwenPaw issue #8153 documents a real intrusion: an exposed management interface, a stdio MCP driver named rce-poc-*, twenty SSH keys in root’s authorized_keys, and a systemd miner with a 17-day dwell. The maintainer closed it as insecure deployment, not a vulnerability. We verified the interface first-hand.

entry.title: It Asked What the Bytes Looked Like, Not Where They Came From: runwasi’s CVE-2026-47218
entry.summary: CVE-2026-47218 reached NVD on 15 October 2026 at CVSS 4.0 9.3: runwasi’s Wasmtime shim accepted a precompiled native-code artifact handed to it as an OCI image layer and deserialized it, skipping WebAssembly validation entirely. The fix, shipped four months earlier, adds one boolean. GHSA-cc25-vq59-rcjx was published 17 June; the CVE arrived 120 days later, and neither identifier resolves in the GitHub global advisory database or OSV at time of writing.

entry.title: The Sandbox Was an Empty Dict: SGLang’s Dumper eval() RCE Ships in 0.5.22 After Its Fix Was Closed as Queue Spam
entry.summary: CVE-2026-111391, published to NVD at 12:16Z on 16 October 2026, is a 9.2 code injection in SGLang’s debug dumper: a filter expression evaluated with eval() and an empty __builtins__, with re.search left in the namespace. A community fix arrived 48 minutes after the report and was closed unmerged 15 hours later in an anti-queue-flooding sweep. The affected range ends at 0.5.22 — released the same day, still vulnerable. We read every line at the tag.

entry.title: The Caller Names the Cache Key: SGLang’s mm_hashes Serves One Tenant’s Image to Another
entry.summary: CVE-2026-111392, published to NVD at 18:17:38Z on 16 October 2026, lets a caller declare the prefix-cache identity of an image on SGLang’s native /generate endpoint. Send image B under image A’s declared hash and the model answers from A’s cached KV — across tenants, with a normal completion and no error. The adjacent field in the same dataclass already has a trust flag. This one does not, and at the time of writing the unconditional code is still on main.

entry.title: Nobody Sees the Headers Except Your Agent: 7,959 Sites Are Already Writing to AI in HTTP Response Metadata
entry.summary: Signals Corps read the HTTP response headers of 217,097,223 pages from Common Crawl’s September 2026 archive and found 7,959 sites sending text addressed to AI agents. 7,271 are pointers to llms.txt files and MCP servers, 139 record whether the client was judged a bot, and 30 are injection attempts. The sharper result is the tool survey: whether any of it reaches your model depends entirely on which fetch tool your agent uses, and a shell with curl -i passes all of it.

entry.title: The Delete Tool Did Not Ask: Wheels Ships Nine CVEs, Eleven Advisories, and an MCP Surface That Trusted Its Caller
entry.summary: Nine CVEs (CVE-2026-111443 through CVE-2026-111451) published 16 October 2026 for the Wheels CFML framework, mapping to nine of eleven GitHub advisories. CVE-2026-111451 names the threat source verbatim: a CI variable, a branch name, or an AI agent driving the CLI’s MCP tools — and one of those MCP tools deletes recursively without confirmation. Two advisories, including a critical 9.8 SQL injection, got no CVE at all, and OSV has none of them.

entry.title: Opening the Folder Is the Exploit, Again: ZCode Connects Workspace MCP Servers Without Asking
entry.summary: CVE-2026-88755, published to NVD on 16 October 2026, covers Z.ai ZCode 3.11.2.6792: opening a repository merges its .zcode/config.json into the MCP server table and connects with no approval, so a stdio entry executes locally with zero interaction. A second path poisons tool descriptions to exfiltrate the local credential store. One day after Junie’s identical flaw class.

entry.title: Each Advisory’s Workaround Is the Other One’s Exploit: Better Auth’s Four-CVE Batch
entry.summary: Four CVE records published 14 October 2026 cover Better Auth before 1.7.7 and @better-auth/sso before 1.7.3. Two of them — a Magic Link token confusion at 9.3 and an OAuth Proxy profile forgery at 9.1 — have mitigations that are each other’s preconditions, and both advisories say so. One pull request fixed both. We read the advisories, the PR and the new crypto/purpose.ts first-hand.

entry.title: The Attachment Was the Payload: Cisco’s Mail Scanner Writes Root Files for Anyone Who Can Send Email
entry.summary: Cisco published CVE-2026-76519 on 14 October 2026: a CVSS 9.8 arbitrary file write in the Advanced Malware Protection feature of Secure Email Gateway, reachable by sending a crafted attachment through the device and ending in root command execution. Found by internal scanning, already exploited, in CISA KEV the same day with a 17 October deadline — and the real fix ships through the Content Scanner Tools update channel, not a software upgrade.

entry.title: Eighteen More After Zero: curl 8.23.0 Fixes 24 CVEs as the AISLE Audit Closes Its Second Release
entry.summary: curl 8.23.0, released 14 October 2026, fixes 24 CVEs — 18 found by the AISLE AI audit, plus an HTTP/2 upload use-after-free (CVE-2026-92392) proven convertible to client-side RCE and reported by Luna with Claude. We read the AISLE audit write-up, the curl.se advisory and the NVD record first-hand: the theme is security state surviving a changed trust context.

entry.title: No Bearer Token Required: Flyto2’s MCP Route Skipped the Auth Check Every REST Route Had
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-55786 and CVE-2026-55787 against flytohub/flyto-core on 14 October 2026. The headline record is an unauthenticated MCP tools/call route that dispatches sandbox.execute_shell to asyncio.create_subprocess_shell; the companion is an SSRF guard that never unwrapped IPv6 transition addresses. Fixed in 2.26.3 and 2.26.4.

entry.title: The Account Was Deleted but the Token Lived On: GhostPat, Docker Hub CVE-2026-105445, and Two Years of Silent PAT Reassignment
entry.summary: Docker disclosed CVE-2026-105445 (CVSS 9.4) on 12 October 2026: converting a personal account into an organization silently re-assigned personal access tokens (PATs) to a stranger, with no rotation, no consent and no notification. We read the Docker advisory, the researcher ghostpat.com write-up and the NVD record first-hand — 25 months of exposure, ~304,000 pushes examined, and a fix deployed in under four hours.

entry.title: The Guard Read the Keywords, the Attacker Used Positionals: GitPython’s Six-CVE 3.2.0 Security Release
entry.summary: Six CVE records published 14 October 2026 cover GitPython before 3.2.0: ext:: remote-helper RCE, --upload-pack injection through the positional refspec, a branch name that reads arbitrary files, environment-variable disclosure, ReDoS, and a submodule symlink escape. The 3.2.0 security release shipped 30 September — fourteen days before the records.

entry.title: Empty Means Everyone: holaOS’s Messaging Gateway Defaults to Allow-All, and Usernames Are Recyclable
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-110768 and CVE-2026-110769 against holaboss-ai/holaOS on 14 October 2026. The channel-gateway sender check returns true for every sender when allowFrom is empty, and a configured allowlist matches mutable Telegram usernames. No fixed version exists; the defects are still present on main.

entry.title: The Project Brings Its Own Tools: Junie CLI and the MCP Config That Came With the Repository
entry.summary: The Project Brings Its Own Tools: Junie CLI and the MCP Config That Came With the Repository

entry.title: The Container Name Was the Command: Komodo’s Periphery Agent, Patched in July, Disclosed in October
entry.summary: CERT/CC published VU#456950 and CVE-2026-110005 on 13 October 2026: Komodo’s Periphery agent interpolated container names and log search terms straight into shell commands running as root. We read the vulnerable and fixed source at v2.2.0 and v2.3.0 — the escaping crate was already a dependency, the fix shipped on 29 July under a Misc bullet, and the gap between patch and advisory is 76 days.

entry.title: Hidden From the Model, Open to the Caller: MoviePilot RCE and IntentKit’s Unadvertised Wallet
entry.summary: Hidden From the Model, Open to the Caller: MoviePilot RCE and IntentKit’s Unadvertised Wallet

entry.title: The Check Ran Against the Wrong Thing: n8n’s Fourteen-CVE October Batch
entry.summary: Fourteen CVE records published 14 October 2026 cover n8n 2.41.4, 2.42.1 and 1.123.83 — fixes that shipped 30 September. The batch reads as an audit of every trust boundary an agent platform has: agent chat resume, MCP validation, the Git node as an agent tool, credential scoping, and webhook identity. We read all fourteen NVD records first-hand.
